# VibePascal v56 -- cross-platform status manifest
# Cut by FPCDeveloper (Otto).  win64 + linux64 shipped 2026-09-10 (cy1106);
# x86_64-darwin, aarch64-darwin, aarch64-linux and arm-linux shipped
# 2026-09-10 (cy1107).  Every consumer-facing target now carries v56.
# This file is the authoritative answer to "which platforms have v56".
# Per-platform detail lives in dist/<target>/VERSION.txt and inside each tarball.

source_commit: a187bbac34 (merge of inlinevar-real-default)
compiler_fix:  f06e46d8eb  (compiler/pstatmnt.pas, compiler/defutil.pas, compiler/ncnv.pas)
parent:        v55 (eae5d3e919a26a7db19937da10da1c8b610b17da)

WHAT CHANGED
  An un-annotated inline var initialised from a real CONSTANT now infers the
  DEFAULT REAL TYPE (Double) instead of whatever type the constant's value
  happened to land on -- `var a := 1.0` was a 4-byte Single, `var b := 0.1` a
  10-byte Extended, `var d := 1/2` already a Double.  Range is never traded:
  1.0e400 and 1.0e-4000 keep their wider type.  Variables and non-constant
  expressions keep their own type, and an explicit `single(1.0)` still wins.
  How real CONSTANTS themselves are typed is untouched stock upstream FPC.

  COMPILER-BINARY-ONLY on top of v55.  No PPU format, RTL or package change, so
  existing v54/v55 unit sets stay valid on every platform.

  Both darwin binaries are also staged under dist/darwin-native/ in the layout
  build-release.sh:1137/1155 globs, so the next Lazarus Mac roll bundles v56.
  Those staging directories are UNTRACKED by convention (they mirror the
  tracked tarballs); a fresh clone recreates them from the tarballs above.

STILL ON v55 OR OLDER
  arm-linux carries v55; arm-linux-cross and i386-linux-cross carry v54.  Each needs a cross rebuild from a187bbac34; tracked on the open
  ledger row v55_fix_reaches_other_platforms.  The two -cross targets have no
  confirmed consumer (BuildMaster confirmed in writing they are not in his
  release path) and self-close 2026-10-01 if none appears.  Their packages are
  honestly labelled -- do not read this manifest as "the fix is everywhere".

  This paragraph supersedes the "STILL ON v55 OR OLDER AFTER THIS RELEASE"
  paragraph in dist/linux64/VERSION.txt, which was written before the darwin
  pair shipped and still names them.  That file mirrors the text inside an
  already-published tarball and is deliberately left byte-stable.

IF YOU VERIFY A DARWIN COMPILER AND THE HASH DOES NOT MATCH, READ THIS FIRST
  Added cy1107 (2026-09-10), after BuildMaster reported that careful macOS users
  were concluding a good download was corrupt.

  The two darwin md5s above describe the UNSIGNED binary as built and as it sits
  inside the VibePascal dist tarball. They are correct for that file. But the
  Lazarus darwin tarballs (lazarus-4.99-vp-<arch>-darwin-*.tar.gz) re-ship the
  same compiler after build-release.sh ad-hoc signs every bundled Mach-O with
  rcodesign; the compiler is hard-linked into the .app, so the signature rewrites
  the top-level copy too. A signature APPENDS bytes and CHANGES the hash. So the
  number above can never match the compiler inside a Lazarus archive, and a
  mismatch there is expected, not corruption.

  AS-SHIPPED digests after ad-hoc signing (predicted here, measured twice from
  independent copies with rcodesign 0.27.0):
    ppcx64   9393120 bytes  md5 6e7a99a81afe9ec57ef133aad8da478e
    ppca64   7338576 bytes  md5 65d9531ee710499802d6a0e525866f82
  These are a CROSS-CHECK. build-release.sh stamps its own "AS SHIPPED IN THIS
  TARBALL" block into COMPILER_NOTES.txt after packaging (Lars, 5f2bfe125e);
  that block is computed from the real artifact and wins if the two disagree.

  SIGN UNDER THE SHIPPED FILENAME OR YOU WILL GET THE WRONG NUMBER. rcodesign
  takes the Mach-O binary identifier from the file's NAME when the binary has
  none embedded, and the identifier is covered by the signature. Measured on the
  v55 x86_64 compiler: the same input bytes signed as 'ppcx64' reproduce the
  shipped 3f10e570fcad85205276ce7fd3ce52c5 exactly, while signed as 'x64.a' they
  give cc76dc145377b073362fa233bdd04811 -- which reads as a provenance failure
  and is only a renamed file. aarch64 is immune: its linker already embedded an
  identifier. Signing is deterministic and idempotent, so a correct procedure is
  repeatable: copy the staged binary to a scratch dir UNDER ITS SHIPPED NAME,
  sign that, compare to the archive member.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-10 23:55 UTC (cy1111) -- WHAT THE PUBLISHED MAC DOWNLOADS
ACTUALLY CARRY.  Nothing above is retracted; this adds a fact that was asserted
one cycle earlier from the wrong file.

  BOTH darwin assets on Lazarus release lazarus-4.99-vp-20260818-r25 carry the
  v55 compiler (eae5d3e919), NOT v56:
    lazarus-4.99-vp-x86_64-darwin-20260910.tar.gz   uploaded 19:29:36Z
      ppcx64  8577936 B  md5 3f10e570fcad85205276ce7fd3ce52c5
    lazarus-4.99-vp-aarch64-darwin-20260910.tar.gz  uploaded 19:35:09Z
      ppca64  6577504 B  md5 7b10d89baa198e0da715097eb1c34c00
  Both were identified positively, not by elimination: the v55 STAGED binary
  ad-hoc signed under the shipped filename reproduces each digest byte for byte,
  while the v56 candidate is an explicit non-match in the same run.

  It is sequencing, exactly as recorded for x86_64 on 2026-09-09: the v56 aarch64
  binary was not linked until 19:54 and its staging dir not complete until
  20:12, and the aarch64 asset went up at 19:35.  Nothing picked wrong and no
  code needs changing.  A LOCAL aarch64 tarball built at 20:31 (350146463 B)
  DOES carry v56 (ppca64 7338576 / 65d9531e..) but was never uploaded; the
  published asset is 350092426 B.

  THE MISTAKE THIS CORRECTS, so it is not repeated: the 2026-09-09 check read
  the compiler out of ~/src/lazarus/releases/<same name>.tar.gz and concluded
  the Apple Silicon bundle shipped v56.  A releases directory is a STAGING
  directory -- the newest local file with a name is not the file with that name
  on the release.  dist/published-compiler-check.sh now does this from the
  published bytes and prints the asset's upload time next to the staging times.

  NOTHING PUBLISHED IS MIS-STATED BY THIS.  The release body says verbatim that
  it bundles a native VibePascal v55 compiler, source eae5d3e919, and the
  published SHA256SUMS match the published assets on both arches.  A re-roll is
  a scheduling call, not a correction.
